thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Mixed as Tech Props up Nasdaq, Dow Losses Traction

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Wall Street Mixed as Tech Props up Nasdaq, Dow Losses Traction
text:
Shutterstock photo Friday's jobs-fueled rally ran into resistance Tuesday as investors contemplated the potentially negative fallout from US/China/Mexico trade issues and rising inflationary pressures in today's services sector data. The Dow closed marginally lower, having failed to hold onto modest gains late in the day, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both closed higher for a third straight day.
The technology sector was the main driver of a new high in the Nasdaq, with shares of Twitter ( TWTR ) at record levels after it was announced that the social media company would replace Monsanto ( MON ) in the S&P 500. Neflix ( NFLX ) will take Monsanto's place in the S&P 100. Apple ( AAPL ) also set an all-time high on tailwinds from Monday's well-received Worldwide Developer's Conference, powering the Nasdaq to a record high.
The services sector of the economy was in focus the purchasing manager's and Institute for Supply Management indices indicating further expansion. The ISM non-manufacturing index rose to 58.6 in May from 56.8 beating the 58.0 consensus estimate. But the impact was dulled by signs of inflationary pressures as the prices paid index swelled to 64.3 from 61.8, its 27th consecutive monthly advance.
Additionally, job vacancies were at an all-time high of 6.698 million according to the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). This also exceeded estimates of 6.54 million available jobs.
In commodities, oil reclaimed some earlier lost ground tied to reports that President Trump urged Saudi Arabia to boost oil production by a million barrels per day. Brent crude futures fell to a 4-week low before recovering lost ground and closing out the day only modestly lower.
Gold snapped a three-day losing streak as the risk-off trade in equities lured investors to the precious metal, driving up its price by $4,, while Treasuries were also buoyed by risk aversion as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note retreated back to 2.91% from 2.93% on Monday.
Wednesday's economic calendar includes the US trade deficit for April and first quarter non-farm productivity and unit labor costs.
